subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should `config.patch` silently discard the four legacy accessor-method property names even though ordinary own-property writes to those names are not treated as prototype pollution elsewhere?
rationale: This is a deliberate security-versus-compatibility policy choice: source inspection establishes the behavior, but cannot determine whether rejecting legitimate plugin or user map keys is an accepted product contract.

options.title: Split out the denylist
options.body: Remove the four accessor-shaped names from the merge-patch filter and land the remaining bounded hardening without changing config compatibility.

options.title: Approve the stricter boundary
options.body: Keep the denylist, explicitly accept silent omission as the config contract, and add focused compatibility or upgrade documentation and tests.

options.title: Pause the combined patch
options.body: Hold the PR until the config hardening can be redesigned or submitted separately from the Control UI and media fixes.

recommendation.title: Split out the denylist
recommendation.body: Remove the four accessor-shaped names from the merge-patch filter and land the remaining bounded hardening without changing config compatibility.
